title: Outlook and Teams down: the Microsoft 365 outage, hour by hour
dek: What broke, when (in India time), what Microsoft has said, and what still works.
bigLabel: Problem reports for Outlook on Downdetector at the peak, around midnight IST on 12–13 Nov

glance.what: From late on 12 November (India time), Microsoft's Exchange Online servers began failing, taking down Outlook email and parts of Teams, SharePoint and Copilot worldwide. Servers that came back kept failing again under traffic.
glance.why: Microsoft 365 runs email and meetings for millions of companies, schools and government offices, including in India. Courts lost live feeds and Australian agencies were hit.
glance.next: As of Microsoft's latest updates on the morning of 13 November (India time), recovery was partial and not sustained. It has not given a time for a full fix or a final cause.

forYou: If you use Outlook for work or college, email may be delayed rather than lost, Microsoft says. Teams chat and meetings mostly work; calendar and scheduling may fail. Microsoft posts official updates on its @MSFT365Status account on X.

upcoming.label: Soon
upcoming.text: Microsoft's all-clear and its explanation of the cause

next: Microsoft's all-clear, and its explanation of what went wrong.

events.title: Microsoft starts investigating email problems
events.summary: Shortly before 1 pm US Eastern time, Microsoft says it is investigating reports of users unable to reach Exchange Online mailboxes in the Americas. It soon says users in any region could be affected.

events.title: Outage spreads across Microsoft 365
events.summary: Microsoft opens a wider incident at 1:26 pm ET: customers may be unable to connect to Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, Copilot and Defender XDR. Outlook problem reports on Downdetector reach about 130,000.

events.title: A first fix brings some servers back
events.summary: Microsoft says it has validated a different way of running server health checks, bringing some servers back online. It says it has found no recent change linked to the start of the problem; its investigation points to a component that processes server health checks.

events.title: Restored servers fail again
events.summary: Microsoft says servers it returned to service can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic. It pauses deployments, limits some traffic to the affected systems and keeps restarting servers.

events.title: No sustained recovery yet; not a cyber attack
events.summary: As Europe wakes up, the outage is still widespread. Microsoft says its fixes are bringing partial recovery but not a sustained one, and a Microsoft executive says it was not caused by a cyber attack. No time is given for a full fix.
